intro: A running list of my research, talks, podcasts, and media. I'm a PhD student in Dynamical Neuroscience at UC Santa Barbara, working in the Bionic Vision Lab on visual prosthetics and accessible technology. If something here is out of date or missing, let me know.

items.title: Aligning visual prosthetic development with implantee needs
items.authors: Lucas Nadolskis*, Lily M. Turkstra*, Ebenezer Larnyo, Michael Beyeler
items.desc: An interview study with Argus II and Orion implant recipients, revealing the gap between researcher expectations and implantees' real-world experiences. (* equal contribution)

items.title: Data Navigator: An Accessibility-Centered Data Navigation Toolkit
items.authors: Frank Elavsky, Lucas Nadolskis, Dominik Moritz
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics, 30(1):803–813 (IEEE VIS)
items.desc: A JavaScript toolkit for accessible, multi-modal navigation of data structures and visualizations via screen reader, keyboard, speech, and gesture.

items.title: VisionAI — Shopping Assistance for People with Vision Impairments
items.authors: Anika Arora, Lucas Nadolskis, Michael Beyeler, Misha Sra
items.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality (ISMAR-Adjunct)
items.desc: A mobile app to enhance the in-store shopping experience for people with vision impairments.

items.title: Navigating the last mile: Evaluating head- and cane-mounted cameras for egocentric spatial awareness
items.authors: Apurv Varshney, Lucas Nadolskis, Tobias Höllerer, Michael Beyeler
items.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality (ISMAR)
items.desc: Evaluates combining head- and cane-mounted cameras to support spatial awareness and last-mile navigation for blind users.

items.title: Use of Computer Vision to Develop a Device to Assist Visually Impaired People with Social Distance
items.authors: Lucas G. Nadolskis
items.venue: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 35(18):15974–15975 (Undergraduate Consortium)
items.desc: A COVID-era assistive computer-vision device to help blind and low-vision people maintain social distance.

items.title: Beyond Sight: Probing Alignment Between Image Models and Blind V1
items.authors: J. Granley*, G. Pogoncheff*, A. Rodil, L. Soo, L. M. Turkstra, L. G. Nadolskis, A. Alfaro Saez, C. Soto Sanchez, E. Fernandez Jover, M. Beyeler
items.desc: Compares evoked neural activity in the V1 of a blind human with a cortical implant against deep neural network representations.

items.title: Sustained stimulus-selective multi-unit activity in human primary visual cortex
items.authors: L. Nadolskis, G. Pogoncheff, J. Granley, A. Rodil, L. Soo, L. Turkstra, et al.
items.desc: Conference abstract on multi-unit recordings in human V1 with a cortical visual implant.

items.title: Exploring top-down visual pathways using micro-stimulation and its applications to cortical visual prosthesis
items.authors: Lucas Nadolskis
items.venue: Carnegie Mellon University — MS Thesis (advisor: Matthew Smith)
items.desc: Master's thesis on top-down visual pathways and their application to cortical visual prostheses.

items.title: NeuroAI Models of the Visual System (Project Lead)
items.authors: Bionic Vision Lab, UC Santa Barbara
items.desc: I lead this project on understanding the visual system in health and disease to inform neuroengineering and visual prostheses.

items.title: Towards a Smart Bionic Eye (Project Affiliate)
items.authors: Bionic Vision Lab, UC Santa Barbara
items.desc: Building practical, useful artificial vision now, rather than waiting to restore natural sight.

items.title: Understanding the Information Needs of People Who Are Blind or Visually Impaired
items.authors: Bionic Vision Lab, UC Santa Barbara
items.desc: Studying the strategies blind and low-vision people use for daily activities to guide future accessibility aids.

items.title: Assistive Technologies for People Who Are Blind
items.authors: Bionic Vision Lab, UC Santa Barbara
items.desc: Integrating computer vision into assistive devices to improve urban navigation and environmental interaction.

items.title: The Vision of a Blind Scientist: Journey, Challenges, and the Future of Visual Prostheses
items.authors: Lucas Gil Nadolskis & Michael Beyeler
items.venue: 11th World Blindness Summit, São Paulo, Brazil
items.desc: Invited talk at the World Blindness Summit on my path as a blind scientist and the future of visual prostheses.

items.title: 2nd Workshop on Accessible Data Visualization (AccessViz) — Organizing Committee
items.authors: with Brianna Wimer, Frank Elavsky, Dominik Moritz, et al.
items.desc: Co-organizer of the second workshop on accessible data visualization at IEEE VIS.

items.title: 1st Workshop on Accessible Data Visualization (AccessViz) — Organizing Committee
items.authors: with Brianna Wimer, Laura South, Frank Elavsky, Dominik Moritz, et al.
items.venue: IEEE VIS 2024, St. Pete Beach, Florida
items.desc: Co-organizer of the inaugural workshop on accessible data visualization at IEEE VIS.

items.title: Assistive device for social distancing for blind users (3-minute pitch)
items.authors: Lucas Gil Nadolskis
items.desc: My undergraduate research pitch on a depth-camera device to help blind users keep social distance.

items.title: How Does Vision Work?
items.authors: Tumble Science Podcast for Kids
items.desc: A kid-friendly episode where I explain how vision works in the brain and whether sight without eyes is possible.

items.title: Towards a Smart Bionic Eye
items.authors: with Michael Beyeler & Jason Esterhuizen
items.venue: NNLM Discovery Podcast (National Library of Medicine)
items.desc: On the Smart Bionic Eye project, navigation as a blind person, and designing implants that complement the cane.

items.title: NeurodiverCity — An 'eye-opening' conversation on bathrooms
items.authors: with Dr. Kirsten Day
items.venue: What is the Future for Cities? (Ep. 200P)
items.desc: A panel discussion on neurodiversity in cities, sensory experiences, and accessible design.

items.title: At a Loss for a McCartney Ticket
items.authors: Lucas Nadolskis
items.venue: The Santa Barbara Independent — Letter to the Editor
items.desc: A letter on being shut out of buying Paul McCartney tickets because the AXS website was incompatible with my screen reader — and the case for digital accessibility.

items.title: A Fan's Dream Comes True
items.authors: The Santa Barbara Independent
items.desc: The follow-up: after my letter, Paul McCartney's team reached out and made sure I got front-row seats to the show.

items.title: A Future Where Blindness Is No Barrier: The Smart Bionic Eye

items.desc: An NLM blog post on the Smart Bionic Eye, with an audio-described video and quotes from me.
